functional_semantics.triton: y = exp(x - m)/l per row with m the exact row max and l the rescaled sum, output in x's dtype (impl_triton.py 20-37).
functional_semantics.cutile: y = exp(tile - m)/l per row with the same m/l recurrence, output in x's dtype (impl_cutile.py 35-61).
functional_semantics.note: Both realise torch.softmax(x, dim=-1) (impl_torch.py 4) for a 2-D input; both unpack exactly two dims (53 / 69).

stages.triton: One kernel, one program per row (grid n_rows, 55): sweep A online max/sum (22-29), sweep B normalise (32-37).
stages.cutile: One kernel, one CTA per row (grid (n_rows,1,1), 71): pass 1 online max/sum (38-49), pass 2 normalise (52-61).
stages.note: Identical single-launch two-sweep online structure; both re-read the row for the second sweep.

dependencies.triton: m, l are program-private scalars consumed by sweep B; rows independent (20-21, 36).
dependencies.cutile: m, l are CTA-private 0-d fp32 tiles consumed by pass 2; rows independent (35-36, 59).
dependencies.note: Per-row statistics before normalisation, no global intermediate, on both sides.

reduction_scan_sort.triton: Per chunk tl.max then tl.sum of exp(x - m_new); sequential rescale l = l*exp(m - m_new) + ... across chunks; -inf padding in sweep A (25-29).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: Per tile ct.max then ct.sum of exp(tile - m_new); same sequential rescale; NEG_INF padding in pass 1 (41-48).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Same online-softmax recurrence with identical initial state (m=-inf, l=0); intra-tile reduction order left to the compiler on both sides.

precision.triton: Loads upcast .to(tl.float32) (25, 35); m, l, exp and division fp32; explicit cast to the output element type at the store (37).
precision.cutile: Loads upcast ct.astype(ct.float32) (43, 57); m, l fp32 0-d tiles; ct.exp and true division; one ct.astype to the output dtype (60).
precision.note: fp32 statistics and exponentials with a single downcast on both sides; plain exp and true division on both.

preprocessing.cutile: torch.empty_like(x); n_tiles = ceil(n_cols/block) computed on the host and passed as ConstInt (70, 97-100).
preprocessing.note: Only the output allocation plus host integer arithmetic inside run() on both sides; no copy, cast or cached state.

mutation.triton: x read-only; fresh output each call (54).
mutation.cutile: x read-only; fresh output each call (70); tuning launches overwrite output (89), rewritten by the final launch.
mutation.note: No input mutation; idempotent; the contract forbids mutation.

hardware_dispatch.cutile: No hardware branches; _HANG_CFGS (15-21) only prunes the tuning space.
hardware_dispatch.note: Single code path on both sides.

fq_boundary.note: Both timed run() bodies allocate the output and launch one kernel; no clone, zero-fill, scratch or cached prepack. bytes_expr (config.yaml 18) is the minimal one-read-one-write bound; both kernels re-read each row for the second sweep, so issued traffic is up to 3x the model when the re-read misses cache. flops_expr is the nominal one-operation-per-element convention.
